title: Every persistence-writer tick re-upserts the whole ~19.9 MB app_state metadata JSON, so the host writes ~1.3 GB per 95 s and drives the NVMe to saturation around admissions
outcome: The host persists app_state metadata incrementally or only when it changes, instead of re-serializing and upserting the whole ~19.9 MB JSON on every writer tick. Host write volume and disk busy time during normal turn admission drop by a measured amount. Every existing durability fence and its exact semantics are preserved.
acceptance: A note identifies every production metadata reader/writer and its storage-unit mapping with file:line. Deterministic fixtures at documented observed entity counts exercise the real persistence path; their sizes and assumptions are explicitly labeled modeled, not a measured production field breakdown. Bounded per-field byte/count diagnostics are included in the change; the observed production19.9MB field distribution remains unknown until collected through the supported diagnostics during the authorized C4 post-change observation. No separate diagnostic landing or direct live-store access is required.

With the fix, a writer tick whose metadata is unchanged writes no metadata bytes, and a tick that changes one session writes bytes proportional to that change, not the whole document. Deterministic tests show both, and show that every durability fence that waited on the old upsert is still satisfied only after its own data is durable.
Reload after crash or restart reproduces the exact same state as before the change. A round-trip test covers fresh, migrated and partially written stores, with no data loss.
A read-only re-measurement on the running host, with the same method as the 2026-10-23 17:41Z capture, records the per-tick metadata bytes and termal.exe write volume before and after.
Focused tests, the full gate and an independent Codex + Claude pair pass, with no outstanding in-scope Medium or higher.
